source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

Meet Sadie! Please welcome our newest Bogan staff member, Sadie! Sadie is Dr. Cannon's dog. Sadie is fully trained and certified as a therapy dog through AAAIP, which is affiliated with Pet Partners. She is also an AKC certified Good Citizen! Sadie took her therapy evaluation test at Bogan, so the evaluator was able to make sure that she is a good fit to work in elementary schools.Sadie is going to start visiting Bogan once a week. She will visit and spend time with our students and staff. Students will always have the choice of whether or not they would like to interact with or pet Sadie.

title: Understanding Alphabet Learning in Kindergarten
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Title 

Talk Title Talk

How Important is the Alphabet?The alphabet is very important! The alphabet is the foundation or building block for reading, writing, and spelling. It is important for each child to recognize and name all the letters and combinations of letters in and out of order and also the sounds associated with them, to be successful with literacy.In Kindergarten, students are taught the letter sounds in conjunction with the letter names. For example, a teacher might say, “Today we are learning the letter that says /b/. What are some words that have the /b/ sound? This is the letter that spells the /b/ sound. It is called the letter b. This is how we make the letter b.” It helps students to connect sounds to known words, as this helps develop a memory aid.As students begin to recognize the letters and understand their sounds, they are able to begin reading and writing independently. This emergent reading begins in Kindergarten (or preschool) and continues through the elementary school years.  It is also important for early learners to know the symbols or ways we write the letters or combinations of letters or graphemes that represent sounds. A combination of 1,2,3, or 4 graphemes can represent a phoneme or sound. For example: 1 letter p, 2 letters ch, 3 letters igh, 4 letters tion. Recognizing letters, sounds, and combinations of letters and sounds is a skill that is needed to read unfamiliar words independently. As students progress in their knowledge of the alphabet and phonics, they are directly and explicitly taught the more advanced letter-sound relationships in a progression from least difficult to more difficult. This instruction continues through the early elementary years. What can I do to help my student?Read to/and with your child every dayRequest a copy of alphabet flash cardsMatching games for uppercase and lowercase lettersCar games could include saying a word, and your child has to tell you what the beginning sound of the word is, then progress to ending sounds. The ultimate goal is that your child can tell you all the sounds in the word.

summary: The alphabet is the foundation for reading, writing, and spelling success. In Kindergarten, students learn letter names, sounds, and letter combinations (graphemes) through explicit instruction that progresses from simple to more complex. **Parents can help** by reading with their child daily, using alphabet flash cards, playing matching games with uppercase and lowercase letters, and practicing sound identification games in the car.

title: 3rd Grade State Testing Information
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Around 

Bogan Around Bogan

3rd Grade Testing Our 3rd grade students will take the fall English Language Arts Ohio State Test this month. Students will test on Wednesday, October 21st and Thursday, October 22nd. We will complete makeups during this week as well. All testing will begin at 9:30am. If possible, please avoid scheduling appointments on these two mornings. If you are a 3rd grade parent, we would LOVE for you to write a letter or card of encouragement to your child that they will read before starting the test. If possible, please put the letters in an envelope because we would like for them to be a sweet surprise for our students!We have planned a (short) 3rd grade Pep Rally on Monday, October 19th for our students. The purpose of this pep rally is to build confidence and encouragement.Teachers are also taking time to explain to students what trying their best looks like when taking a test. For example, we encourage students to take their time and check their work. We would appreciate if you would also talk to your student about the importance of doing their best on the test. Students who do their best on the test will be invited to a 3rd grade Movie Party on Thursday, October 29th!

summary: **3rd grade students will take the fall English Language Arts Ohio State Test on Wednesday, October 21st and Thursday, October 22nd, beginning at 9:30am.** Parents are encouraged to write letters of encouragement for their children to read before testing and to avoid scheduling appointments on these mornings. A 3rd grade Pep Rally will be held Monday, October 19th, and students who do their best on the test will be invited to a Movie Party on Thursday, October 29th. **Testing tips include:** get plenty of rest, be on time, eat a good breakfast, relax and take a deep breath, and follow your teacher's directions.
